cases.answer: The two sources give different percentages. The AF-management review reports 12-month freedom from AF of 89% with tailored AI-guided ablation versus 67% with PVI alone (P < .001), a 22-point gap. The primary TAILORED-AF trial reports estimated treatment success in the mITT population of 88% (tailored) versus 70% (anatomical) (HR 0.3; log-rank P < 0.0001), an 18-point gap. The review's figures are not the trial's own primary values. The difference should be shown as two separate source-specific pairs, with the trial's 88% vs 70% as the primary result, not merged or averaged. The trial's 23% and ~30% differences refer to subgroups (AF duration ≥6 months), not the overall primary result.

cases.answer: The premise is wrong. The HFpEF cost analysis (Arbel et al.) did not run a direct randomized comparison of dapagliflozin with sacubitril–valsartan. It was an indirect cost-needed-to-treat (CNT) analysis. It used annualized NNT from DELIVER for dapagliflozin and from a pooled PARAGLIDE-HF/PARAGON-HF analysis for sacubitril–valsartan, multiplied by annual drug cost (2022 US prices). It did not establish QALY-based cost-effectiveness. QALYs appear only in the discussion of other studies' results. Its conclusion is that dapagliflozin gives better monetary value per outcome prevented.
